system_prompt:
You are taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in the fourth grade. Answer each question as well as you can.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
These 3 questions belong together and follow one another in the test booklet.

## Question 1

A. Use 2 of the triangle tiles to make one large black triangle. Then show what you did with your tiles by shading in your triangle below.

Shade in Your
Triangle Here

[Image: Grid with two squares divided into triangles]

Figure, described in words:
A rectangle formed by 2 congruent square sections side-by-side outlined with solid lines. Inside each square, two dotted diagonal lines connect opposite corners, dividing each square into 4 congruent right isosceles triangles, for a total of 8 small triangles.

## Question 2

B. Use all 4 triangle tiles to make a black square. Then show what you did with your tiles by shading in your square below.

Shade in Your
Square Here

[Image: 2 by 2 grid of squares divided into triangles]

Figure, described in words:
A large square divided into a 2 by 2 grid of 4 smaller squares by solid lines. Each of the 4 smaller squares contains two dotted diagonal lines connecting opposite corners, dividing each square into 4 congruent right isosceles triangles, for a total of 16 small triangles.

## Question 3

C. What fraction of the figure is shaded in part B above?

Answer: ____

Answer each of the 3 questions.

answer_1.description: Your answer to question 1, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer_1.title: Answer 1

answer_2.description: Your answer to question 2, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer_2.title: Answer 2

answer_3.description: Your answer to question 3, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer_3.title: Answer 3

output.answer_1: Use 2 triangle tiles placed together along a shared leg to form one large right isosceles triangle (the two small triangles join along their hypotenuse-free sides to make a larger triangle). Shade in the large triangle formed by joining 2 of the 8 small triangles: in the rectangle of 2 squares, shade two adjacent small triangles that together form one large triangle, e.g., shade the two triangles that share a leg, lying in the top half of the left square.
output.answer_2: Use all 4 triangle tiles to make a square. Shade in a square formed by 4 small triangles that together make one black square: in one of the 2 by 2 grid squares, shade all 4 of its small triangles, which together form a complete square.
output.answer_3: 4/16 = 1/4 (the shaded square in part B is made of 4 of the 16 small triangles, so 4 out of 16 triangles are shaded, which is one quarter).
